title: Remarks at Zanesville, Ohio
paragraphs: I shan't make a speech I am coming back to see Ohio later, and this time I am simply going down to the Firemen's Convention at Chattanooga. I have a pretty good opinion of railway men, and I believe most of you have. All I shall do will be to thank you warmly for coming here to greet me, and I know you will not grudge my [?] saying that I prize it most of all in the men who wear the button that shows that they fought in the great war. Good luck to you. (Applause)
